section_entries.mathematical_role: Transforms the sums into cotangent contour integrals, scales them to phase-amplitude form, analyzes saddle geometry, and identifies the dominant exponential rate.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Stirling scaling separates phase and amplitude and decomposes the integral by frequencies
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: After scaling by n and applying Stirling’s formula, the contour integral is expressed through an exponential phase and amplitude. A polynomial identity for the trigonometric factor decomposes it into frequency-indexed integrals whose saddle equation becomes an algebraic root problem.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A second saddle regime sharpens coefficient growth estimates
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Crude derivative bounds first control all rational coefficients, then auxiliary horizontal contour integrals and a saddle associated with a minimal imaginary root sharpen their exponential growth rate. This supplies the coefficient-size budget required by the later independence criterion and distinguishes it from the saddle controlling linear-form smallness.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The proof strategy is a tunable balance among prime-adic denominator saving, exponential smallness of the linear form, and exponential growth of its coefficients; irrationality or dimension gain appears only when the combined rate crosses the criterion’s strict threshold.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a structural synthesis of the paper’s dependency chain, not an independently verified general criterion; exact rates and signs remain scan/PDF dependent.
related_synthesis_entries.title: The three-budget irrationality engine

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The saddle selected for decay of the linear form and the imaginary-root saddle used to bound coefficient growth encode distinct sides of the same construction, making their rate comparison more informative than either asymptotic in isolation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The relationship is supported within this source’s construction; it should not be generalized to other irrationality methods without separate evidence.

risk_spans.reason: Page header and whitespace before Lemma 4.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Stationary points do not contribute equally. A root-separation hypothesis classifies the admissible saddles on a closed level curve, contour deformation places each frequency integral through its unique saddle, and Laplace asymptotics reduce the competition to the outer relevant modes; their maximal real phase determines the exponential decay rate of the original linear forms.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Under condition (19) on the nearest real root μ_1 beyond c, Lemma 4 lists all solutions of f′(τ)=λπi in the right half-plane and places them on a smooth closed curve defined by Re(f′)=0, with sign information inside and outside. The contours M_λ are deformed through the corresponding saddles. Lemma 5 applies Laplace's method to give the exponential magnitude of J_{n,λ}; Lemma 6 then identifies the limsup rate κ of I_n and explains which outer odd-frequency modes govern it.
directed.conceptual_reading: The geometry supplies both admissibility and selection: it proves uniqueness along each frequency and orders saddle contributions by real phase. Dominance is therefore a consequence of the level-curve structure, not simply choosing the visually largest stationary point.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is root condition → saddle classification and level curve → contour deformation → Laplace estimate for each J_{n,λ} → maximization over the modes actually present in the decomposition → exponential rate κ for the linear form.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The root-separation inequality, contour shapes, radicals, phase normalization, dominant indices, and rate formula are diagram- and formula-sensitive. The qualitative selection mechanism is reliable, but exact hypotheses and constants require the PDF.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty about geometric details and dominant-mode indexing; high uncertainty about the exact rate expression.

supported: Under condition (19) on the nearest real root beyond c, Lemma 4 classifies all right-half-plane solutions of f'(tau)=lambda pi i, places them on a smooth closed level curve, and gives sign information inside and outside it.
The source deforms each mode contour through its corresponding unique saddle and applies Laplace's method in Lemma 5.
Lemma 6 identifies the limsup exponential magnitude rate kappa of I_n and shows that the outer modes actually present—lambda=±1 when b=1 and lambda=±(b-2) when b>1—control the result.
inference: The candidate accurately explains that the level-curve geometry establishes admissibility, uniqueness, and ordering rather than allowing a saddle to be selected heuristically.
Maximization of the real phase among modes present in the cosine-polynomial decomposition is the correct selection mechanism.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous reading calls kappa an 'exponential decay rate' of the original linear forms, but Lemma 6 establishes an exponential magnitude rate; it need not represent decay before the normalization and denominator balance imposed in the final argument.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Outer relevant modes' is acceptable only with the explicit qualification that the top formal coefficient c_b vanishes for b>1, leaving ±(b-2) as the outer modes actually present.
context_or_ocr_risk: The root-separation inequality, level-curve geometry, contour parametrization, dominant indices, and rate formula are highly diagram- and formula-sensitive.
revision_instructions: Replace 'exponential decay rate' with 'exponential magnitude rate'.
State separately that effective smallness is obtained only after combining this rate with denominator saving and normalization in the final criterion.
